messages:
alix: Quick summary from the late-night run: deployed tenant-aware mixed-capacity pool in us-west1. baseline cost down ~62% vs pure on-demand, but we hit a couple of surprising eviction cascades during spot drains.
benji: Nice! what was the min on-demand floor you enforced?
alix: We set a conservative per-region floor of 12% reserved on-demand, plus per-tenant override that pins critical tenants to 30% when their monthly commit > $50k.
dana: How are we enforcing tenant isolation when bursting to spot? worried about noisy neighbors and KV-cache thrash.
alix: Two parts: 1) runtime pins KV-cache to on-demand VMs for active sessions, 2) bursted spot tasks run with a read-through cache and warmup pipeline. If a spot goes away, we route in-flight requests to on-demand shadow instances and replay the minimal prefix to rebuild session state.
ekaterina: Any network issues observed? I remember earlier tests where cross-AZ cache fetches blew up because of new VPC egress rules.
alix: Yup — one of the cascades was because the failover path required short-lived cross-AZ requests to the warmup pool. New egress ACLs throttled them and that delayed handoff ~6s, which multiplied latencies for small-chat workloads.
mohammed: Can we avoid cross-AZ during handoff? e.g., pre-warm in the same AZ as the tenant's routed on-demand nodes?
alix: That's the plan. Proposed changes: pre-warm burst slots per-AZ with a tiny standing pool (2-4 instances) that are always hot for warmup traffic; make handoff purely AZ-local unless AZ is depleted.
benji: Sounds good. How about the eviction detection latency? The cloud drain notice sometimes comes <30s.
ekaterina: We tuned our drain hook to act on scheduled-interruption metadata + spot-price-surge signal. autoscale-bot posted a 30s-before-drain event and a 10s-final event in the run.
autoscale-bot: [event] spot-drain-us-west1-a detected for instance i-0abcde at +00:00:30 — initiating graceful migrate.
mohammed: For the graceful migrate, are we doing any token-level accounting or cost attribution to tenants during replay? We need accurate billing if a tenant consumed on-demand during a forced failover.
dana: We tag the shadow instance with the original tenant_id and emit event lines for billing pipeline. Example log: 
```
[eviction] tenant=redwood-pro id=tp-42 src=spot-123 dest=od-77 replay_tokens=48 cause=preemptible-drain
```
benji: Nice. Edge case: what if the on-demand floor itself gets exhausted (e.g., region-wide outage), then what? Do we degrade non-critical tenants first?
alix: Yes — hierarchical fallback: 1) intrazon handoff to on-demand floor per-tenant, 2) if insufficient, drop to per-customer SLAs: we throttle or degrade low-tier tenants (LRU prompt dropping + compressive quantization), 3) if still insufficient, fail open to lower-cost model variant (smaller model) with label in response.
ekaterina: We should codify the ordering in a runbook. Also add a metric: "eviction_handoff_latency_p50/p95" and "tenant_fallback_count" per-tenant.
mohammed: Agreed. Also add a circuit-breaker that prevents more than N concurrent replays per-AZ to avoid storming the warmup pool.
dana: One more operational note — the cost math: with 12% region floor + 2-4 prewarm per-AZ we're paying a steady-state delta. but it reduces p95 tail and avoids cold-start churn which was the main hidden cost.
alix: I ran a backtest: adding AZ prewarm increased steady cost by ~3.2% but reduced eviction-related latencies and replay token spend by ~28%. ROI looks good for PLG tiers above X.
enki: (oops not in participants)
benji: Action items: 1) draft runbook for tenant-aware handoff + priority list (dana) 2) implement AZ-local prewarm flag + autoscale-bot annotation (ekaterina) 3) add metrics and billing tags for replay events (mohammed) 4) safety circuit-breaker for replays (alix) 5) test in eu-west1 next (benji)
alix: I'll add the config snippet to the infra repo tonight:
```yaml
mixed_pool:
  region_floor_pct: 12
  per_tenant_overrides:
    enterprise_threshold: 50000
    enterprise_floor_pct: 30
  az_prewarm:
    enabled: true
    min_instances_per_az: 2
  handoff:
    az_local_only: true
    max_concurrent_replays_per_az: 6
```
dana: sgtm. Also add a short note about VPC egress rules — need an exception for ephemeral warmup fetches.
ekaterina: I'll open the change request for the ACL and schedule a small canary test next week.
mohammed: I'm adding billing tags to the replay pipeline now.
autoscale-bot: [task] runbook created: /infra/runbooks/tenant-eviction-handoff.md
benji: Thanks all — let's keep the canary tight and observe both cost and p95. :thumbsup:
